chunks: And from him, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who raises the place of his forehead in the mosque (i.e., lifts it slightly off the ground during prostration). He said, 'I love to place my face in the place of my foot,' and he disliked it.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: mosque (here referring to the place of prostration)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on lifting the forehead slightly during prostration in prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the etiquette of prostration by expressing a preference for the face to be placed directly in the spot previously occupied by the foot, emphasizing complete humility and full contact with the ground. He explicitly disliked the act of lifting the forehead, which was a known practice among some worshippers, thereby establishing a normative standard for the physical manifestation of submission (khushu) in prayer.
